items.prompt: Black to move. White's pawn on b5 and the knight on g5 both press. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) rates Black's h6, Ng4, Ne8 and d5 all within 0.7 pawns of the best.
c5 is worse than the best move by at least 60 centipawns.

hints: Do not decide with the pawn first: ask which of your moves keeps the position open and which locks it.
Four moves are close: a pawn move that attacks the knight on g5, two knight moves (Ng4 and Ne8), and a central break.
The pawn on the h-file attacks the knight; the central break uses the d-pawn.
items.explain: Black's knight on f6 and pawn on e4 need room; a move that attacks the white knight, or a break in the centre, keeps the position open. The pawn move that closes the queenside is clearly worse [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.c6c5: The pawn closes the queenside for ever. White's knights get a square on d5 that no black pawn can attack, and the engine rates the move at least 0.6 pawns worse than the good moves (about 0.8 at depth 16).

items.prompt: Black has played ...Kh8. White to move. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Nd5.
Bh5 is worse than the best move by at least 130 centipawns.
The square d5 is an outpost for White: supported by a pawn and attackable by no black pawn.

hints: Look for a square that no black pawn can attack.
After the pawn went to c5, the square in front of the d-pawn is supported by White's c-pawn and cannot be challenged by a pawn.
The c3 knight goes to d5.
items.explain: The square d5 is supported by the pawn on c4 and no black pawn can attack it any more, so no black pawn can chase a white piece away from it; the piece can only be traded, which costs Black time and still leaves White the pawn on d5. The engine rates the knight jump far ahead of the other moves [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.e2h5: A bishop move that wins nothing; the engine rates it 1.3 pawns worse than occupying the outpost.

items.prompt: White to move after 16...c5. The queenside is closed. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers a4, Rb1.
Rf1 is worse than the best move by at least 100 centipawns.

hints: Black has closed the wing with a pawn. Which side now has the space to expand on it?
White's own queenside pawns can now advance without a black pawn to stop them.
The a-pawn or the rook goes to the b-file.
items.explain: With the queenside closed, White can advance there at leisure and keep the outpost on d5 in reserve; a pawn advance or a rook to the b-file both fit that plan, and the engine rates a quiet rook move clearly lower [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.e1f1: A rook move on the first rank starts no plan; the engine rates it 1.0 pawns worse than a queenside advance.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight has retreated to h3. Choose a move that keeps the position open.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) rates d5 and Ng4 within 0.4 pawns of the best.
c5 is worse than the best move by at least 100 centipawns.
After the move one black pawn (on d5) attacks c4.

hints: The knight has left g5, so the h-pawn has done its job. What is the next open-position idea?
A pawn break in the centre attacks White's c-pawn.
The d-pawn moves two squares, or a knight jumps to g4.
items.explain: The break on d5 attacks the pawn on c4 and keeps the position open; the engine rates it first, with Ng4 about 0.2 pawns behind [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.c6c5: Even now the pawn move c5 closes the queenside; the engine rates it at least 1.0 pawns worse than the central break (about 1.2 at depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move. Both sides have a plan. Choose a move that keeps Black's plan on schedule.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers g5, h5.
a6 is worse than the best move by at least 30 centipawns.

hints: Count the moves each side needs for its plan. A move that is not part of either plan loses a tempo.
Both good moves are pawn moves on the kingside.
The g-pawn or the h-pawn advances.
items.explain: White's plan (the c-pawn break) needs a few moves; Black's pawn storm needs about as many. A quiet rook-pawn move starts neither plan and gives White a tempo; depth 16 rates it about 0.4 pawns behind the two pawn advances, which is inside the few-tenths noise of a single reading [V, weak]. [I] Which tempo matters depends on who is faster, so count before you choose.

feedback_by_move.a7a6: A quiet queenside move: it loses a tempo in the race. The engine rates it about 0.4 pawns worse than the pawn advance, a small gap that is within the noise of one reading; two such moves cost more.

items.prompt: Black to move, one pawn move from the storm. Both sides have a plan. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers g4, Qe7.
Qe8 is worse than the best move by at least 50 centipawns.

hints: Ask which move brings a new piece or pawn to the plan instead of retreating.
Two moves are close: the pawn that starts the storm, and a queen move that adds protection.
The g-pawn advances, or the queen goes to e7.
items.explain: The pawn on g5 can advance to g4 and attack the pawn on f3; the queen on e7 keeps the position together. A retreat to e8 does neither [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.d8e8: The queen goes backwards and helps neither the storm nor the defence; the engine rates it 0.5 pawns worse than the two good moves.

items.prompt: White to move. Black threatens to open the kingside with ...g3. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Nc5, Rc6.
Kf1 is worse than the best move by at least 40 centipawns.

hints: Do not defend a threat that a counter-threat can answer: look for a piece move that attacks something.
The knight on b7 and the rook on b3 can both start an attack on the black pieces.
The knight jumps to c5, or the rook moves up the board.
items.explain: Against a pawn storm the quiet king move answers no threat and starts no plan. On f1 the king stays on the f-file, where the pawn that arrives on g3 attacks the bishop on f2 and the pawn on h2 with tempo. The knight jump and the rook move are the engine's first choices; the king step is about half a pawn behind [V, depth 16: at least 0.4]. Paraphrasing Znosko-Borovsky: against a time lead keep making threats of your own [V-sheet].

feedback_by_move.g1f1: The king step is slow and the engine rates it at least 0.4 pawns worse than the counter-strikes (about 0.5 at depth 16): it answers no threat and leaves the pawn storm alone.

items.prompt: Black to move, a knight down for a pawn. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers f3.
g3 is worse than the best move by at least 90 centipawns.
After the move one black pawn (on f3) attacks e2.

hints: You have given material. Which pawn move keeps the attack alive and attacks two white units?
The pawn on f4 can advance to a square where it attacks the bishop on e2 and the pawn on g2.
The f-pawn advances.
items.explain: The pawn on f3 attacks the bishop on e2 and the pawn on g2, so White must react to it. It is the only move that keeps the king-side attack alive, and the engine rates the alternatives far lower [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.g4g3: A second pawn thrust gives White time to take it; the engine rates it 0.9 pawns worse than the pawn on f3.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's pawn on f3 attacks two white units. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Bb5.
Qb3 is worse than the best move by at least 130 centipawns.

hints: When the opponent attacks two units with a pawn, look for a reply that attacks something bigger.
A move that saves the attacked piece and makes a threat beats a pure retreat.
The bishop on e2 moves along the diagonal to b5.
items.explain: The bishop steps out of the pawn's attack with a threat on the queen on e8, so White loses no time; the engine rates it far ahead of the quiet queen moves [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.b4b3: The queen retreats and does not hit anything; the engine rates it at least 1.3 pawns worse than the bishop move (about 1.6 at depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move, worse. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers e3.
Qa6 is worse than the best move by at least 80 centipawns.

hints: When you are worse, ask what your best piece or pawn still attacks. Which black pawn is deep in White's camp?
Look at the pawn on f3 and the pawn on e4: can one of them advance and attack something?
The pawn goes to e3 and attacks the queen on d2.
items.explain: Black's queen is attacked, but the pawn on f3 still cramps White's king. A pawn thrust that opens lines keeps the initiative; the engine rates it ahead of the queen retreat [V, depth 16]. When you are worse, an active repair often beats a passive one [I].

feedback_by_move.c4a6: The queen retreats and the engine rates it 0.8 pawns worse than the pawn push; White has time to untangle.

items.prompt: Black to move; the queen on c4 is attacked by the bishop on b3. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Qg4.
Qa6 is worse than the best move by at least 190 centipawns.

hints: Where can the queen go and still point at White's king?
The pawn on f3 and the queen on the fourth rank work together.
The queen goes to g4, next to the white king's pawns.
items.explain: The queen on g4 stays near White's king and together with the pawn on f3 keeps the threat of mate alive; the engine rates it far ahead of the other retreats [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.c4a6: The queen retreats far from the king; the engine rates it at least 1.9 pawns worse than the queen move to g4 (about 2.3 at depth 16).

items.prompt: White to move. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers a7.
Rxe5 is worse than the best move by at least 290 centipawns.
Exactly one black piece (the pawn on f6) defends the bishop on e5.

hints: Ask what each tempting move allows before you play it.
Two ideas tempt: take the bishop, or push the pawn. Count the defenders of the bishop on e5 before you capture it.
The a-pawn advances one square and attacks the rook on b8.
items.explain: The pawn on f6 defends the bishop, so taking it wins nothing. The pawn move attacks the rook on b8 and threatens to queen; the engine rates it first by a wide margin, and every other move is worse by about two pawns [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.e1e5: The bishop is defended by the pawn on f6, so the capture only swaps a rook for a bishop; the engine rates it at least 2.9 pawns worse than the pawn move (about 3.4 at depth 16).
